LESSON: FORCE AND ITS EFFECT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 3.1: Force and its effect
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Force and its effect, part of Force and Energy in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How does force affect objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Force and its effect together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner uses digital devices with assistive technology to search for uses of force in day-to-day life

● Communication and collaboration: The learner develops communication skills as they discuss ways of minimising friction

between moving bodies.

Values:
● Love: The learner cares for one another as they work in groups to carry out activities that demonstrate the existence of force

of gravity and force of friction in nature.

● Unity: The learner exercises inclusion as they brainstorm on the meaning of the term force as used in science.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: The learner exercises leadership as they work in groups while discussing the application of force of friction and

force of gravity in day-to-day life.

Link to other learning area:

Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner relates the concepts of force of friction in maintenance farm tools and equipment.
